catalyst_observation.source_statement: FDA CRL for LIQ861 (NDA seeking approval for PAH) stated the FDA is 'unable to approve the NDA at this time,' citing CMC data on the drug product and device biocompatibility, plus a reconfirmed need for on-site pre-approval facility inspections (COVID-19 travel restrictions had prevented them during the initial review cycle). The CRL did not cite need for additional clinical, toxicology, or clinical pharmacology studies - a CMC/facilities-focused rejection, comparable in kind to the already-pooled REG-2024-RCKT-KRESLADI-CRL, but still an unambiguous NDA rejection and approval delay (issuer's own release: 'FDA...has issued a complete response letter'). LIQ861 was eventually approved as Yutrepia in 2025 after further CRLs and litigation, none of which is inspected or referenced here - only the November 2020 CRL's own first-public disclosure is used.
